newsitem.title: GERMANY: German retail giants discuss joint lobby group.
newsitem.headline: German retail giants discuss joint lobby group.

text.p: Two of Germany's top store groups, Metro AG and Karstadt AG, said on Friday they were discussing forming a joint lobby group to better represent retail interests.
The two companies said in a common statement that, despite differing interests among retailers, "It is worthwhile to promote cooperation and represent a common position in the public arena."
Metro, Europe's biggest retailer, and department store group Karstadt said they had held talks on Thursday over how to go about forming a single umbrella organisation.
"The goals of cutting costs, improving efficiency and increasing political clout are shared by many retailers," a Metro spokesman told Reuters.
Germany has an alphabet soup of retail lobby groups -- including the HDE, which groups smaller shops, the BAG lobby of larger stores and the BFS club of self-service outlets.

But the organisations have often been at cross-purposes -- especially over the recent loosening of decades-old laws restricting store opening hours. Small stores opposed the move, while the larger retailers were in favour.

In the event, many retailers were poorly prepared for the extension of store hours last November and failed to capitalise over the all-important Christmas shopping season. The year 1996 ended as the fourth in a row of stagnant retail sales.
Earlier, Metro said it was pulling out of the BAG, while Karstadt said it would quit the HDE. Karstadt chief executive Walter Deuss has also said he would stand down as chairman of the BAG.
